title: Associativity of finite pro-etale derived pullback comparisons
statement:
Let $j:W\to Z$, $h:Z\to Y$, and $k:Y\to X$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Fix a finite commutative ring $A$, with constant coefficient sheaves $A_T$ on their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and canonical coefficient identifications [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Let $Lf^*$ be the ordinary unbounded derived module pullback [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Write $c_{f,g}:L(g\circ f)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*\circ Lg^*$ for the comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], with the canonical constant coefficient identifications; its source is the pullback $L(g\circ f)^*$ formed with the canonical identification of the composite, which agrees with the composite identification required by that lemma by [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition]. For every $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_X)$ the equality
$$Lj^*(c_{h,k}(M))\circ c_{j,k\circ h}(M)=c_{j,h}(Lk^*M)\circ c_{h\circ j,k}(M):L(k\circ h\circ j)^*M\longrightarrow Lj^*Lh^*Lk^*M$$
holds after the canonical functor associator. The comparisons are the ones normalized by the termwise module pullback maps on K-flat complexes with flat terms in the cited composition lemma; no arbitrary choice of composition isomorphisms is allowed.
